subject.title: Bug: Gateway falsely marks healthy local vLLM endpoints as timed out/overloaded, causing 1–23 min fallback cascades

question: What current-main live vLLM/Gateway trace is sufficient to decide whether the remaining healthy-endpoint false-timeout and `sessions_spawn` latency cascade still reproduces, and should this stay one canonical issue while that trace is gathered?
rationale: The source shows several plausible owner boundaries and already-landed partial fixes, but the remaining reported behavior cannot be safely accepted as fixed or assigned to a single code path without maintainer-owned timing proof.

options.title: Keep Canonical Pending Live Trace
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical healthy-vLLM timeout cascade item and require a fresh trace before any repair PR.

options.title: Split After Reproduction
options.body: Use the next trace to split confirmed timeout, auth-profile, cron/live-session, and Gateway RPC symptoms into narrower follow-ups.

options.title: Close As Partial Fixes Enough
options.body: Close only if maintainers accept that the remaining timeout symptoms are covered by docs/config and adjacent fixes without a current-main repro.

recommendation.title: Keep Canonical Pending Live Trace
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical healthy-vLLM timeout cascade item and require a fresh trace before any repair PR.

likelyOwner.reason: osolmaz is the live assignee and merged adjacent cron fallback work on the same provider/fallback decision surface.
